lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Add a product-focused headline or brief introduction.
items.because: Without one, a quick reader has to infer your target role from the experience section.

items.says: Put the strongest product outcomes before lower-level operational work within the Harbor role.
items.because: The onboarding and checkout achievements are stronger for a PM application than ticket triage.

items.says: Make sure the professional-profile link is a real, polished URL rather than a placeholder.
Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: Neither is needed for a U.S. résumé, and they can introduce bias or privacy concerns.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is complete.
items.because: Its status should be unambiguous, particularly after the listed June 2025 end date.

items.says: Specify whether the 35% conversion change is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: The result needs a clear definition.

items.says: Give the measurement period and explain how the conversion result was evaluated.
items.because: A reviewer may question how the lift was measured.

items.says: Keep the “for all merchants” scope only if it is accurate and supportable.
items.because: It is a broad claim.

items.says: Clarify the dispute self-service feature’s scope or intended outcome.
items.because: Shipping early says more about schedule than product impact.

items.says: Make clear that $1.1 million is an estimate of annual losses.
Make the basis for the chargeback-loss estimate defensible.
Clarify the period behind the 140 tickets and queue reduction.
Explain what the opt-in comparison established and its limitations, or combine it with the onboarding result.
items.because: The bullet gives a method but no result, and merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not.

items.says: Specify the time period for the 9-to-4-day onboarding result.
Make the pilot-region scope of the 2,300 merchants clear.
Avoid attributing the improvement to the redesign unless the evaluation supports it.
items.because: An opt-in comparison cannot establish that the redesign caused the improvement.

items.says: The late-delivery reduction comes from excluding weather-delayed shipments rather than improving delivery performance.
items.because: Changing how performance is counted may look like gaming the metric.

items.says: Add a reliable before-and-after period or downstream impact if available.
items.because: It would make the pick-error result easier to assess.

items.says: “Prepares” is inconsistent with the past-dated role.
items.because: The bullet’s verb tense should match the role dates.

items.says: Show what the S&OP work changed or enabled.
items.because: The bullet describes a recurring responsibility without an outcome.

items.says: Clarify the period or basis for the 1,800 annual driver hours saved.
Explain how the 9 tonnes of food were measured.
Give “in its first year” a clear referent.
Consider adding a reliable indicator of participation or service impact.
items.because: It could strengthen the result.

items.says: Clarify the length of the “following term.”
Do not imply the reminders alone caused active-user growth unless that was measured.
Vary the repeated use of “launched” across the project’s first two bullets.
items.because: It makes the project sound more repetitive than it is.

items.says: Give “95% of pickup slots” a clear denominator.
Make clear that the staff-cover-shift figures use comparable periods.
Add the analysis, recommendation, decision, or deliverable from the working sessions.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity, not an outcome.

items.says: Use active wording that makes your contribution clear.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your role.

items.says: Quantify how much the form changed or what improved, if reliable data is available.
items.because: “Shortened” and “adopted” leave the result vague.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result is misplaced under the hospital practicum and duplicates the Harbor achievement.
items.because: It does not fit the project and undermines confidence in the résumé’s accuracy.

items.says: Substantiate the broad product-skills list with the experience bullets.
List A/B testing only if you have designed or analyzed controlled experiments.
items.because: The opt-in comparison does not establish that you ran an A/B test.

items.says: Consider adding other tools or methods you can credibly discuss.
items.because: The tools section is brief.
